column1: # *** APOLANT'S 8.1.1791 IS CONFIRMED BY THE ACT ITSELF, 15 September 2026. ***
# DGS 8166578 image 2687: "En ocho dias del Mes de Enero de 1791 anos", in arabic numerals.
# *** Ficha 355 was right about the date. It was also right about Felix Lerena and Rosalia Aguilar. ***
# *** It was WRONG about the bride's father: the note said "Ramon Fernandez Tresguerras"; the act
# says RODRIGO Fernandez, which is also what the 1811 baptism says. *** See data/1791-marriage-act.tsv.
# *** THE TREE THAT CARRIES "AGUILAR" NAMES A DIFFERENT COUPLE - 14 September 2026, and it overturns
# this morning's Granada hypothesis. *** FamilySearch blocked this session with "Access Denied - Error 15",
# so the 1791 act could not be chased on its own films. Geneanet was open, and the jfina tree - one of the
# four this archive cites for the form "Lerena y Aguilar" - turns out to carry a long sourced note that
# answers more than the act would have. Transcribed in full below, and then argued with.
what
column4: what it does to this archive

column1: *** SANCHO'S PARENTS ARE FELIX LERENA AND ROSALIA AGUILAR ***
column2: Geneanet, tree of jfina (Josefina Sanchez Abal), individual 3082: "Sancho Lerena y Aguilar, *** Born in 1767 - Cordoba Andalucia ***, Deceased in 1832. *** Parents: FELIX LERENA, ROSALIA AGUILAR ***"
column3: SECONDARY - a user tree, but a sourced one
column4: *** THIS REFUTES THE GRANADA HYPOTHESIS THIS ARCHIVE BUILT THIS MORNING. *** The reasoning then was that "Lerena y Aguilar" must mean a son of SANCHO DE LERENA Y ARMENTA and ANA MARIA DE AGUILAR, married at Granada in 1754 - so that Aguilar was a GRANDMOTHER's name. *** It is his MOTHER's name. *** Rosalia Aguilar, married to Felix Lerena. That is ordinary Spanish naming and it needs no Granada at all. *** And it explains the null: *** the controlled search for children of the Granada couple returned nothing not because the index is thin but because this man is not their son.

column1: *** THE 8 JANUARY 1791 DATE HAS A PUBLISHED SOURCE, AND IT IS NAMED ***
column2: The same note: "Nacido en Cordoba, Andalucia por 1767, h. de Feliz Lerena y Rosalia Aguilar, *** c.m. 8.1.1791 *** ... h. de Ramon Fernandez Tresguerras y Rosa Fernandez *** (Apolant, "Operativo Patagonia ...." ficha 355) ***"
column3: SECONDARY - *** but published, numbered and citable ***
column4: *** For three days this archive has carried "married at Canelones, 8 January 1791" as a thing "the trees say". It is not. It descends from JUAN ALEJANDRO APOLANT, "Operativo Patagonia: historia de la mayor aportacion demografica masiva a la Banda Oriental, con la nomina completa, filiaciones y destino de las familias pobladoras" (Montevideo, Imprenta Letras, 1970), FICHA 355. *** A named work with a numbered entry is a different order of thing from a hobbyist's assertion. *** It is now an OBTAINABLE document rather than a rumour. ***

column1: *** AND THE PLACE IS NOT IN IT. THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN ADDING "CANELONES" ITSELF ***
column2: The note gives the date and then "Consejo de Morcin, Asturias". *** That is the BRIDE'S ORIGIN, not the wedding's. *** Her own page proves it: "Josefa Fernandez Tresguerras, *** Born in 1778 - Concello de Morcin. Asturias ***"
column4: *** The DATE has a published source. THE PLACE HAS NONE. *** Every file here that says "Canelones, 8 January 1791" has been welding a sourced date to an unsourced venue and presenting the pair as one claim. *** The venue is an inference - a good one, see the padron row below, but an inference - and it should have been labelled as one. ***

column1: *** WHO THE BRIDE'S FAMILY WERE, AND WHY THE SURNAME IS IN NO URUGUAYAN INDEX ***
column2: Josefa born 1778 at *** MORCIN, ASTURIAS ***; her father *** RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, "asturiano" ***; and the source is a book about the *** OPERATIVO PATAGONIA *** - the mass migration of Spanish families shipped to settle Patagonia in 1778-1781 who were largely diverted into the Banda Oriental
column4: *** This answers a question this archive raised and could not solve. *** It searched Uruguayan indexes for TRESGUERRAS and got 83 results, "every one of them fuzzy noise", and concluded the name "is in no Uruguayan index at all". *** Now it is obvious why. They were not a Uruguayan family. They were ASTURIAN COLONISTS OF A SPECIFIC DOCUMENTED CONVOY *** - which is exactly the kind of cohort that has its own published nominal roll and no presence in ordinary local indexes.

column1: *** THE 1812 PADRON IN FULL - AND IT HOLDS THINGS THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE ***
column2: Sancho Lerena fue censado en 1812, en la calle San Juan (hoy Ituzaingo) Nº60, andaluz, 45 años, c/c Maria Fernandez de 36. Hijos: *** Juan Agustin, Pedro Antonio y Fidel, naturales del CANELON", de 21, 19 y 12 años ***. *** Agustina, Justa y Dominga, naturales del "CANELON", de 17, 10 y 7 años ***. *** Su suegro: RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, 63 años, asturiano ***, y *** 4 ESCLAVOS ***. (AGN, Fondo ex AGA, Lº 251, Padron de Montevideo de 1812)"
column3: The padron image was read here on 13 Sep; *** this is its household in full, from a transcription ***
column4: *** THE ARCHIVE HAD SANCHO AND MARIA ON TWO LINES. IT DID NOT HAVE THE OTHER SIX PEOPLE, THE FATHER-IN-LAW, OR THE FOUR ENSLAVED PEOPLE IN THE HOUSE. *** Three things follow. (1) *** ALL SIX CHILDREN ARE "NATURALES DEL CANELON" *** and the eldest is 21, so born about 1791 - the couple were living at Canelones from the year of the marriage, which is the best support the venue has ever had, and it comes from a census rather than a tree. (2) *** RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, the father-in-law, was living in the household *** - the same man the 1812 baptism act calls "DON RODRIGO FERNANDEZ Y TRESGUERRAS". (3) *** This family held four enslaved people in 1812 ***, which this archive has recorded for Pedro Antonio's bakery and had not recorded for Sancho himself.

column1: *** AND IT CORRECTS A "SAID AGAINST MYSELF" THAT WAS SIMPLY BAD ARITHMETIC ***
column2: data/1791-marriage-hunt.tsv says of the 1812 baptism godparents "DON JUAN AGUSTIN SERENA y DOÑA AGUSTINA PERENA": *** "Juan Agustin cannot be Sancho's son, who would be a child in 1812." *** The padron gives *** JUAN AGUSTIN aged 21 *** and *** AGUSTINA aged 17 *** in that very year
column3: *** THE OBJECTION WAS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN ***
column4: *** Sancho's two eldest were 21 and 17 in 1812, not children. *** The godparents at that font were named JUAN AGUSTIN and AGUSTINA; Sancho's eldest son and eldest daughter were named JUAN AGUSTIN and AGUSTINA; and if Maria Josefa was Micaela's sister the pair were the baby's first cousins, which is the most ordinary godparent choice there is. *** So "SERENA" and "PERENA" almost certainly are LERENA, the machine's S-for-L for the sixth time - and the archive talked itself out of a correct reading with an age it never checked. ***

column1: *** A THIRD FORENAME PROBLEM, IN THE SAME SHAPE AS SANCHO-OR-FRANCISCO ***
column2: The tree's CHART calls the bride's father *** RODRIGO *** Fernandez Tresguerras. The tree's NOTE, quoting Apolant, calls him *** RAMON *** Fernandez Tresguerras
column3: Chart and note disagree inside one tree
column4: *** RODRIGO wins on the evidence, 2 to 1: *** the 1812 padron says Rodrigo, and the Montevideo baptism act of 15 May 1812 read here says "DON RODRIGO FERNANDEZ Y TRESGUERRAS". *** Ramon appears once, in a transcription of a transcription. *** Recorded rather than silently dropped, because this archive has been badly served before by assuming the odd one out is the error.

column1: *** DOMINGA IS IN THE CENSUS AND MISSING FROM THE TREE ***
column2: The tree lists seven children and its own prose says "Tuvieron 8 hijos". *** The padron lists DOMINGA, aged 7 in 1812 *** - and she is not among the tree's seven
column4: *** This archive found Dominga Josefa's baptism at Canelones on 15 May 1804 from the act itself. *** The census independently confirms a Dominga of about that age in the household. *** The tree, which is the source of almost everything else on this page, drops her. *** A useful calibration: this tree is well sourced and still incomplete, and the acts read here have already caught one of its gaps.

column1: *** TWO MORE PUBLISHED CITATIONS, NEITHER OF THEM CHASED YET ***
column2: (1) *** "Revista 15 IEGU pag 53-54" *** - Revista del Instituto de Estudios Genealogicos del Uruguay, number 15, pages 53-54. (2) *** "Los Lerena de Canelones aparecen mencionados como persona de confianza del BARON DE LA LAGUNA en 1817, para vigilar 'la seguridad y tranquilidad en la campaña', por Francisco Bauza, "Historia de la Dominacion Española", ed. 1929, III pag 285" ***
column3: REFERENCE - citations read, works not opened
column4: *** The second is a historical placement this archive has never had: the Lerenas of Canelones as trusted men of the BARON DE LA LAGUNA - Carlos Frederico Lecor, the Portuguese governor - in 1817. *** That sits directly beside what this archive already holds about the family under Oribe in the Guerra Grande, and it is thirty years earlier. *** Both works are findable in Uruguayan libraries and neither needs FamilySearch. ***

column1: *** A PROBLEM WITH THE DATE THAT NOBODY HAS RAISED ***
column2: Josefa born *** 1778 ***; married *** 8 January 1791 *** - she would be *** TWELVE OR THIRTEEN ***. The 1812 padron gives her age as 36, so born about 1776, which makes her *** about fifteen ***
column3: Arithmetic on the tree's own numbers
column4: *** Fifteen is young and possible; twelve is not, for a first marriage with a first child in 1792. *** So either the 1778 birth year or the 1791 marriage date is slightly out, and the padron's 36 is the better figure because it comes from a census rather than a reconstruction. *** Recorded as a flag on the 1791 date - which this archive is otherwise about to treat as solid because it now has a published source. A published source can still be wrong. ***

column1: # ================ *** WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE ACT ITSELF *** ================
# *** THE ACT WAS NOT FOUND TODAY AND COULD NOT BE. *** FamilySearch blocked this session outright, and
# that is where the Canelones films are. Nothing here is the act; all of it is about the act.
# *** BUT THE HUNT IS IN A BETTER STATE THAN IT WAS THIS MORNING: ***
#   1. The date 8.1.1791 now traces to APOLANT, "Operativo Patagonia", FICHA 355 - a named published work.
#      *** Obtaining that page is now the cheapest route to whatever Apolant himself cited ***, and he was
#      a serious archival historian who worked from the parish books and the AGN.
#   2. The VENUE has no source at all and this archive should stop writing it as though it did - though
#      the padron's six children "naturales del Canelon", eldest born about 1791, supports it strongly.
#   3. *** GUADALUPE DE CANELONES HAS MARRIAGE BOOKS FROM 1775 ***, so the act exists physically. The
#      archive's earlier note that it is "probably not digitised" rested on a FULL-TEXT search, and full
#      text covers only a fraction of what is filmed. *** Browsable images are a different question and
#      have never been checked. That is the first thing to do when FamilySearch lets this session back in. ***
#   4. *** THE SPANISH SEARCH SHOULD NOW BE FOR FELIX LERENA AND ROSALIA AGUILAR, NOT FOR GRANADA. ***
#      A marriage of Felix Lerena and Rosalia Aguilar, and a baptism of their son Sancho about 1767, both
#      in CORDOBA. That is a completely different search from the one run this morning.
# ================ *** THE SOURCING CHAIN, TRACED ONE STEP FURTHER *** ================
# The pages of FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR were opened on 14 September. *** BOTH ARE EMPTY OF EVERYTHING
# EXCEPT A SOURCE LINE. *** No dates, no places, no other children - only "Sources - Family: *** Revista 15 IEGU ***".
# *** SO THE TWO CLAIMS REST ON DIFFERENT AUTHORITIES, AND THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE IS THE WEAKER. ***
#   - The 1791 marriage and the 1812 padron come from APOLANT, "Operativo Patagonia", ficha 355.
#   - *** SANCHO'S PARENTS come from REVISTA 15 IEGU, pp.53-54, AND FROM NOTHING ELSE. ***
# *** THIS MATTERS BECAUSE THE GRANADA HYPOTHESIS WAS WITHDRAWN ON THE STRENGTH OF THOSE PARENTS. *** The
# withdrawal stands - a tree citing a named journal beats a naming-rule inference - but it should be read for
# what it is: *** one un-consulted article in one journal, reported at second hand by one tree. *** If Revista 15
# turns out not to say it, or to say it without a source, the question reopens. Labelled so rather than treated
# as settled.
# ================ *** AND NEITHER BOOK CAN BE HAD ONLINE *** ================
# Searched on 14 September: *** archive.org holds NEITHER *** Apolant's "Operativo Patagonia" NOR the IEGU
# Revista (its catalogue returns unrelated German medical titles for "Apolant" and radio programmes for
# "Operativo Patagonia"). *** HathiTrust has Operativo Patagonia but serves a bot check *** and, being a 1970
# imprint, would be search-only in any case. *** Both are in-copyright Uruguayan imprints and are LIBRARY OR
# PURCHASE ERRANDS, not things this session can reach. *** Logged as such in data/errands.tsv with full citations.
# *** A TRAP CAUGHT ON THE WAY, AND IT IS THE SAME TRAP IN NEW CLOTHES. *** Three Google Books API searches -
# "Fernandez Tresguerras", "Lerena y Aguilar", "Rosalia Aguilar" - each returned *** totalItems: None ***, which
# reads exactly like a null. *** IT WAS HTTP 429, QUOTA EXCEEDED. *** A control query made the error visible.
# *** Three nulls were within one keystroke of being written into this archive, for the second time this month
# and on a completely different platform. *** The rule generalises beyond FamilySearch: an empty result from any
# API is not evidence until something known-positive comes back through the same call in the same session.
# The IEGU's own holdings list was reached over plain HTTP on 14 September (its HTTPS certificate has expired)
# and it states, for Canelones: *** "3.- CANELONES. Catedral de Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe. Baut. y Matr. desde
# 1775; def. desde 1776. Existen algunas informaciones matrimoniales desde 1776." ***
# *** SO THE ACT EXISTS, THE PARISH IS NAMED, AND THE MARRIAGE BOOKS START SIXTEEN YEARS BEFORE IT. *** This
# archive's earlier verdict that it is "probably not digitised" was about FULL TEXT and was never about the
# document. *** And the informaciones matrimoniales run from 1776 - the same series in which Sancho has already
# been found giving evidence at somebody else's marriage. His own should be in that bundle. ***
# ================ *** SIX TREES, AND THEY ARE NOT SIX WITNESSES *** ================
# Geneanet's index returns *** SIX family trees carrying FELIX LERENA married to ROSALIA AGUILAR ***
# - antoniojosed, rosanaic, jfina, nanabal, ladissosa and abal2018. That looks like strong corroboration
# for the parentage this archive used on 14 September to withdraw the Granada reading. *** IT IS NOT. ***
# Each was opened on 14 September 2026:
#   - *** antoniojosed *** is the only one with dates: Felix born *** about 1725, Cordoba ***; married
#     *** about 1753, Cordoba ***, to Rosalia Aguilar *** about 1729 ***. Every value is "about", there is
#     no Sources section at all, and the only note is "Religion: Cristiana. Nacionalidad: Espana".
#   - *** rosanaic *** gives the same dates and cites, as its source for the birth, *** A LINK TO
#     antoniojosed's TREE. *** It is a copy, and says so.
#   - *** abal2018 *** and *** ladissosa *** carry the couple with NO dates and NO sources.
#   - *** jfina *** carries no dates either, and cites *** Revista 15 IEGU ***.
# *** SO THE SIX REDUCE TO TWO ORIGINS AT MOST: *** one Uruguayan circle (jfina credits "mi primo
# ALEJANDRO ABAL" in its own acknowledgements, and abal2018 and nanabal carry that name) resting on a
# journal article; and one Spanish tree of undated estimates. *** This archive has made exactly this
# mistake before and caught it: *** the three 1846 "Francisco" entries that looked like three witnesses
# were one clerk writing one page on one morning. *** Copies are not corroboration. ***
# *** AND THE TWO CAMPS DISAGREE ABOUT SANCHO'S BIRTH BY THIRTEEN YEARS. *** The Uruguayan trees give
# *** 1767-1832 ***. antoniojosed gives *** ca 1754 ***, which is what you get if you assume a marriage in
# 1753 and a first child the year after. *** The padron of 1812 records him as 45, which is 1767 *** - a
# census against a reconstruction, and the census wins. *** That also makes antoniojosed's "about 1753"
# marriage an ESTIMATE DERIVED FROM A GUESSED BIRTH, not a record of an act. ***
# *** WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THE GRANADA QUESTION: *** for an hour this looked like a real coincidence -
# a Lerena marrying an Aguilar at CORDOBA in 1753, one year before Sancho de Lerena y Armenta married
# Ana Maria de Aguilar at GRANADA in 1754. *** There is no coincidence, because the 1753 is not a date
# from a document. *** It is a tree's arithmetic, and it is arithmetic built on a birth year the census
# contradicts.
# *** WHAT ITEM 2 OF THE FIFTEEN ACTUALLY YIELDED: *** no record of Felix Lerena or Rosalia Aguilar was
# found anywhere - no act, no index entry, no parish. *** Cordoba as their home rests on ONE UNSOURCED
# TREE, and the parentage itself still rests on ONE UNREAD ARTICLE. *** The withdrawal of the Granada
# reading stands, because a journal citation beats a naming-rule inference - but it stands on less than
# a six-tree consensus, and this file now says so plainly.
